en: Taal Volcano sits on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake, making it a volcano within a lake within an island.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, native to Mindanao, is one of the largest and rarest forest raptors globally.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, situated just south of Metro Manila.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippine archipelago, located in the northern part.
The Surigao region in Mindanao contains some of the largest and most economically important nickel deposits worldwide.
The giant Rafflesia, found in the rainforests of Mindanao, produces the largest individual flower on Earth.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage marine sanctuary.
The eastern coasts of the Philippines, particularly in the Bicol Region, frequently experience direct hits from Pacific typhoons.
Indigenous Ifugao people carved the famous Banaue Rice Terraces into the Cordillera mountains over 2,000 years ago.
